title: Region-bound audit capture with tamper-evidence and retention orchestrator
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a production-grade pipeline that captures all admin actions, privileged access events, and config changes with region-scoped residency metadata, enforces configured retention per-customer and per-region, and stores evidence in a tamper-evident write-once backend. The system must support automatic export for compliance auditors, integrity proofs (Merkle-based receipts + HSM signing), and an operator-friendly retention orchestrator that reconciles policy changes without losing evidence or violating residency.

Rationale: Existing audit capture is fragmented (console logs, DB rows, ad-hoc exports). For customers with residency and WORM requirements we need a single authoritative evidence fabric that: (1) guarantees append-only semantics, (2) enforces retention and deletion rules respecting residency and legal holds, (3) exposes cryptographic proofs for integrity checks and exports for auditors, and (4) integrates with console/console APIs and Dedicated/Private deployments.

Scope:
- Capture streams: admin.action, access.grant/revoke, role.change, policy.update, key/material rotation, config.apply, emergency-admin-override.
- Residency tagging: every event must include region attribute and customer residency tag.
- Storage: write-once object sink per-region (S3 Object Lock / on-prem equivalent) + periodic signed Merkle manifests stored separately and mirrored to an immutable ledger.
- Retention orchestrator: policy engine that schedules retention, respects legal holds, and issues retention-compliance reports.
- Exports: per-customer evidence bundles with integrity metadata and verification instructions.
- Operational: monitoring, alerting for failed writes, verification jobs, and retention reconciliation failures.

Non-goals: full multi-tenant encryption key management (we will integrate KMS/HSM per release), analytics on audit content (search/LM inference), long-term archival strategy for >7 years (deferred to follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: All defined event types (admin.action, access.grant/revoke, config.apply, role.change, key.rotate, emergency-override) are emitted to the audit pipeline with region and residency tags
Events are written to a region-scoped write-once storage backend with Object Lock or equivalent and are verifiably append-only
System generates Merkle manifests for daily batches and signs manifests with an HSM-backed key; receipts are queryable via API
Retention orchestrator applies per-customer per-region policies and enforces deletions only when allowed (no deletion under legal hold)
Operator dashboard shows retention state, pending deletions, reconciliation errors, and ingestion lag metrics
Export API returns a tamper-evident bundle (events + manifests + signatures) for a given time window and residency, and the bundle verifies locally using provided instructions
Integration tests simulate region failover and ensure fallback writes to alternate region are recorded and marked with fallback_metadata
Security review completed and threat-model mitigations addressed in the design doc

labels_fulltext: This ticket covers a cross-functional effort (runtime + infra + console + security). We must be careful about export timing, key management for signature verification, and ensuring retention enforcement cannot be bypassed by tenant admins. Consider adding a small retention audit job that samples objects and verifies retention metadata periodically.
notes: 2025-02-18 - Asha: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to use daily Merkle manifests to keep verification overhead low. Target per-region manifests signed and stored in a separate immutable bucket.
2025-02-25 - Diego: Prototype shows 99.98% write success to S3 Object Lock under load; edge-case on eventual consistency for listing requires manifest-driven verification.
2025-03-03 - Security: HSM policy needs to allow signing by an operator role; pending policy doc from Security (ticket created)
2025-03-09 - Evelyn: Implemented initial manifester and sign routine. Integration tests failing on time-skewed events — added event monotonicity ordering in buffer before batch commit.

2025-03-12 - Marcus: Selecting OPA as policy evaluation engine; will implement a thin reconciler that evaluates policy decisions and issues retention tasks. Potential risk: OPA policy eval latency under large customer counts; plan to cache decisions per-customer per-day.
comments: Diego (2025-02-28): PR for S3 writer includes idempotency by event_id and commit-anchor manifest. Needs review for edge-case when object lock retention mismatch occurs.
Priya (2025-03-05): Producers must add legal_hold boolean immediately when an investigation is opened. This will be a product contract we need to document.

Security (2025-03-07): Consider publishing a verification CLI that auditors can run offline given the exported bundle. We should include the signer's public key and instructions to validate the Merkle root and the signature.
Evelyn (2025-03-11): Proposed fallback metadata format: fallback_region, original_write_time, fallback_reason. This will help auditors trace cross-region retries.
Lina (2025-03-12): Console wireframes for retention dashboard uploaded to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1AuditDashboardDraft
